title: A record ID is unique across the workspace
statement: No two records MAY share an ID, of one kind or of two, in any product of the workspace: every ID goes through the record_id registry, and the store refuses one used twice. An ID MUST NOT be reused or renumbered once it has been used, because tests, code and other records cite it.

title: A record ID matches the ID pattern
statement: A record's ID MUST match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)*$`; the registry's check refuses any other. Each kind's convention (its ID pattern in the schema, shown in the reference: product prefix, domain code, then kind code and number) SHOULD be followed, but only the pattern is enforced.

title: Every record but a product has a parent of an allowed kind
statement: A product MUST NOT have a parent: its table has no parent column. Every other record MUST name its parent in one of its kind's parent columns, a foreign key to an existing record of an allowed kind, and following parents MUST NOT lead back to the record. The store refuses a missing, unknown or disallowed parent, and a cycle.

title: A record has every column its kind requires
statement: A record MUST have a non-empty title and a value of the right type for each required column of its kind's table, such as `statement` on a requirement or `file` on a component. The store refuses a row of an unknown table, a column its table lacks, a missing required value and a value of the wrong type.

title: A link points at a record that exists
statement: Every link MUST be a row of its relation's table whose ends are foreign keys to existing records; the store refuses a link to a record that does not exist.

title: A link uses a relation allowed for its source and target kinds
statement: A link MUST join two kinds its relation allows; the store refuses an unknown relation, which has no table, and a pair the relation does not allow, even when the link table's supertype ends accept both kinds.

title: A test's file exists and names the test's ID
statement: An automated test's `file`, relative to the repo root, MUST name a file that exists, and that file MUST contain the test's ID or else every ID of a record the test proves, for example in the test's name; a test with a `key` MUST instead have a file that contains the key text. This is what ties the spec to the code that proves it. A manual or planned test needs no file, but one it names MUST exist. A component's `file` MAY name a file that does not exist yet: that is work still to do, not breakage.

title: Kinds and relations are the schema, not code
statement: Every kind and every relation MUST be a table of the schema with its meta_kind or meta_relation rows, defined by the numbered migrations in `lathe/schema/` or generated from a product's declarations. The engine, the checks and the app MUST NOT hard-code the list of kinds or relations.

title: A product's declarations name only kinds that exist
statement: A product kind's parent kind and folder, and every product relation's source and target kind, MUST name kinds and folders the schema has; each field name MUST be lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. The store refuses the rest, naming the declaration and what it lacks.

title: The about relation allows any kind as its target
statement: A relation whose target is the record_id registry, such as `about` from an open question, MUST allow a link to a record of any kind.

title: Lathe's schema changes only by a migration
statement: Lathe's own kinds, columns and relations MUST change only by a new numbered migration in `lathe/schema/`, reviewed in git. The app, the API and the command layer MUST NOT change the schema: a write to a meta table is refused.

title: Obligations and link roles come only from the schema
statement: Which kinds are obligations and which relations design or prove them MUST come only from the schema's kind obligation and relation role. Coverage and the coverage checks MUST NOT name a kind or relation of their own.

title: A product adds kinds of its own and never widens Lathe's
statement: A product MUST NOT declare a kind with the name of one of Lathe's tables, nor widen one of Lathe's kinds with another parent or more required columns: that takes a migration. Its own kinds MUST come after Lathe's, with their own label, stage, folder and obligation.

title: A product declares each kind once
statement: Each product kind MUST be declared by one product_kind row; the store refuses a second row of the same name, naming its file and line and the line of the first.

title: Each capability in a domain has its own whole-number position
statement: A capability's `position` MUST be a whole number from 1, and no two capabilities in the same domain MAY have the same position; the store refuses either. The position sets the capability's place in the domain, and the domain's use case index lists capabilities in that order.

title: Once a domain has capabilities, each of its use cases belongs to one
statement: When a domain has capabilities, each of its use cases SHOULD sit under one of them. A use case left directly under the domain is work still to do, reported as a warning, not breakage.

title: A pattern's settings have lower-case names
statement: Each setting of a pattern MUST be a pattern_setting row whose name is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter; the store refuses another. A setting is a row of its own, never a column of the record that follows the pattern, so any such name MAY be used.

title: A pattern rule's setting is one of its pattern's settings
statement: The setting a pattern rule depends on, and its applies-when setting, MUST be one of its pattern's settings, so that every use case that follows the pattern answers it; the store refuses another name.

title: An ID in text is plain text, never a link
statement: An ID written in a record's text MUST be kept exactly as written and MUST NOT link, satisfy, prove, apply or otherwise relate one record to another: only a row of a relation's table does that. No check MAY read text for IDs, so an ID in text that no record has, or that names another product's record, is no problem.

title: A relation pair is its relation, source kind and target kind
statement: A relation pair MUST be identified by its relation, source kind and target kind alone; its role, labels and description belong to the relation. A product MUST declare each pair once: the store refuses a pair declared twice, naming its file and line.

title: Each step of a flow has its own position on its path
statement: The steps on each path of a flow MUST each have a different whole-number `position`; the store refuses a repeated position on a path, a position that is not a whole number and a step without one. Steps on different paths MAY share a position.

title: A step carries out only what its flow carries out
statement: What a step fulfills MUST be part of a use case its flow carries out: one of its requirements, a domain rule it applies, or an interaction requirement reached from either or set on the flow.

title: A flow with steps fulfills what its steps fulfill
statement: Once a flow has steps, what it fulfills MUST be the union of what its steps fulfill: each `fulfills` link belongs on the step that does it.

title: A pattern without settings asks nothing of its use cases
statement: A pattern MAY have no settings. A use case that follows a pattern with no settings MUST NOT be asked for any setting value, and a domain that follows a pattern MUST NOT be asked for settings at all.

title: A kind's obligation is full, proof or none
statement: A kind's obligation MUST be `full` (designed, built and proved), `proof` (proved only) or `none`; the schema's enum refuses any other. A product kind declares its own, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs.

title: Pattern rules need proof only
statement: The schema MUST make `pattern_rule` a proof-only obligation, since a real product asks only for proof of the patterns a domain follows. A product MUST NOT change that, since Lathe's kinds cannot be widened.

title: A step may carry out the rules of the patterns its flow follows
statement: A pattern rule MUST count as inside a flow when its pattern is followed by a use case the flow carries out or by the flow's domain, and so MUST an interaction requirement that fulfills such a rule. A step that fulfills any other pattern rule MUST be reported as outside its flow.

title: Folders are data in the schema
statement: The folders kinds sit in, their stage, position, label and description, MUST be rows of meta_section, and each kind's folder its section, so that changing them needs no change to the engine or the app.

title: Every kind's folder is one the schema lists
statement: A kind's folder, when it has one, MUST be one of the schema's folders: a kind's section and a product kind's section are foreign keys, and the store refuses another.

title: A kind's folder belongs to the kind's own stage
statement: A folder that belongs to a stage MUST hold only kinds of that stage: a Define kind sits in a Define folder, a Design kind in a Design folder.

title: A folder of no stage may hold a kind of any stage
statement: A product-level folder, listed with no stage, such as `shared` for patterns and standards, MAY hold a kind of any stage.

title: Layers are records each product names
statement: A domain's layers MUST be records of the `layer` kind, named and ordered by the product, not a fixed list or a field on each component, so that a product chooses its own layers without changing the schema.

title: A layer sits under a domain or another layer
statement: A layer's parent MUST be a domain, or another layer when it is a sub-layer of that layer. A layer is not an obligation.

title: Each layer beside others has its own whole-number position
statement: A layer's `position` MUST be a whole number from 1, and no two layers with the same parent, the domain or the layer that holds them as sub-layers, MAY have the same position. The store refuses a position that is not a whole number, and `layer-order` reports a repeated one. The position sets the layer's place among the layers beside it.

title: Layers in different domains may share a position
statement: Layer positions MUST be compared only within one domain: a layer MAY have the same position as a layer of another domain.

title: Once a domain has layers, each of its components belongs to one
statement: When a domain has layers, each of its components SHOULD sit in one of them. A component left directly under the domain is work still to do, reported as a warning, not breakage.

title: A domain with no layers holds its components itself
statement: A domain with no layers MAY keep its components directly under it, and that MUST NOT be reported.

title: A component in a layer belongs to the layer's domain
statement: A component under a layer, or under a sub-layer at any depth, MUST belong to the layer's domain and product, found by walking its parent chain, everywhere a record's domain matters.

title: A layer changes no coverage
statement: Putting a component in a layer MUST NOT change any domain's coverage: what it designs and builds counts in its domain exactly as when it sits directly under the domain.

title: A layered component designs what its domain owes
statement: A component in a layer MUST design the pattern rules its domain owes, as a component directly under the domain does, and MUST NOT design them for another domain.

title: A layer holds only components and sub-layers
statement: Only components and other layers, as its sub-layers, MAY sit under a layer. Use cases, flows and tests are grouped by capability, and tests by what they prove, not by layer.

title: An entity's role is root or child
statement: An entity's `role` MUST be `root` or `child`: the aggregate's root record, or one of its parts. The schema's enum refuses any other value, and a missing one.

title: An aggregate with entities has exactly one root
statement: An aggregate that has entities MUST have exactly one whose role is `root`; the store's aggregate-root validation refuses none or more than one. An aggregate with no entities needs none.

title: An entity lists its fields as entity_field rows
statement: An entity's fields MUST be its entity_field rows, in position order, each with a name, a meaning and a type, and an example when one helps. An entity with no fields MUST be reported as an `entity-fields` error.

title: Each field of an entity is named once
statement: No two fields of an entity MAY have the same name, compared trimmed and in any letter case; the store refuses a second one.

title: Parts stay inside their aggregate
statement: A `has_one` or `has_many` link MUST join two entities of the same aggregate, because parts belong to their aggregate.

title: A reference may cross aggregates and domains
statement: A `refers_to` link MAY join an entity to an entity of any aggregate of its product, in its own domain or another; it is the only entity link that may leave the aggregate, and like every link it stays inside its product (`LA-AUT-DR75`).

title: Every child entity is reached from its aggregate's root
statement: Each child entity SHOULD be reached from its aggregate's root by `has_one` or `has_many` links inside the aggregate, directly or through other children. `refers_to` links do not reach it.

title: An unreached child is work to do; other entity mistakes break the ERD
statement: A child entity its root does not reach SHOULD be a warning, since the ERD can still be drawn. An entity without fields and a part outside its aggregate MUST be errors, and a bad role or an aggregate without exactly one root MUST be refused by the store.

title: Every table, column and relation is described
statement: Every kind, table, column and relation MUST have a description, since the reference shows it as its meaning: Lathe's as comments in its migrations, a product's in its declarations, which the store refuses without one. Every check row MUST have its summary and explanation.

title: The reference is generated, never kept by hand
statement: The lists of kinds, tables, columns, relations, folders, checks and ID conventions MUST be generated from the schema and the check rows, into `lathe/REFERENCE.md` and `GET /api/reference`, and never written by hand.

title: Each kind's ID convention is data in the schema
statement: Each kind's ID pattern and example MUST be its id_pattern and id_example in the schema; a product kind MAY declare its own.

title: Every relation rule is labeled both ways
statement: Every relation, Lathe's or a product's, MUST have a non-empty `forward_label` and `reverse_label`; the store refuses a product relation without both. Every place that shows a link, in the wiki, the side bar, the graph and the reference, reads it by these words rather than by the relation's name.

title: A product relation never changes Lathe's
statement: A product relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MAY only add a pair whose kinds that relation's link table accepts, and MUST NOT change Lathe's role, labels or description.

title: An event is named in the past tense
statement: A domain event's title MUST say what happened, in the past tense and subject first, such as Loan opened or Loan became overdue. Since only a heuristic can tell, a title with no past form as its last word or after its first SHOULD be reported as a warning, not an error.

title: An event is raised inside its own aggregate
statement: A domain event's `raised_by`, when it has one, MUST name an entity of the event's own aggregate. An event MAY have no `raised_by`, such as one raised by time passing or in an aggregate with no entities.

title: An event lists what it carries as event_field rows
statement: A domain event's fields MUST be its event_field rows, each with a name, a meaning and a type, one name per event compared trimmed and in any letter case, as an entity's are. An event with no fields MUST be reported as an `entity-fields` error naming it as an event.

title: Any aggregate, use case or component may react to an event
statement: A `reacts_to` link MAY go to an event from an aggregate of any domain, a use case or a component; it is the only link that says what happens because of an event.

title: An unheard event is a warning, not an error
statement: A domain event that nothing reacts to SHOULD be reported as a warning that says this can be fine and names what might react, since an event may be kept only for the record.

title: A path is main by default, compared trimmed in any case
statement: A flow step's `path` MUST be compared trimmed and in any letter case, and a step written without one MUST be on the path named main.

title: Each path of a flow is numbered without gaps
statement: The steps of each path of a flow MUST be numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on. A path whose positions skip a number MUST be reported once by `step-order`, on the first step after the first gap, naming every missing number.

title: A domain rule under an entity belongs to its aggregate
statement: A domain rule MAY sit under an entity of its aggregate. It MUST then belong to that aggregate, domain and product, found by walking its parent chain, and every check and coverage MUST count it as a rule directly under the aggregate.

title: A domain is named for a capability, not a technology
statement: A domain MUST be a vertical slice of business capability, named for what it does for someone, with technology as a layer inside its Design stage. A domain whose title or domain code names a technology layer or delivery channel, as a whole word in any letter case (web app, frontend, backend, API, UI, server, database, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, Electron and the like), SHOULD be reported as a `domain-named-for-technology` warning. Its description is not read, since a domain may well say which technologies serve it.

title: A rule across aggregates names the aggregates it involves
statement: A domain rule that holds across aggregates MAY sit directly under its domain, and MUST then name with `involves` the two or more aggregates of that domain it ties together. Such a rule that involves fewer than two aggregates, counting only links to aggregates, SHOULD be a `domain-rule-involves` warning that says to move a one-aggregate rule under that aggregate. Each aggregate of another domain it involves SHOULD be a warning that says a rule across domains is a domain event's job. A domain rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses `involves` SHOULD be a warning, since its place already says what it is about.

title: The reference shown is the product's own
statement: The kinds, relations, folders and checks the reference pages show MUST be the product's own: the schema with its product kinds, and Lathe's check rows with the product's. The pages MUST be built from the loaded data; a check that reports problems but has no row is the engine's own, listed without an explanation.

title: Every kind and every check has one page
statement: Each kind MUST have one page at `/format/kinds/<kind>` and each check one page at `/format/checks/<check>`, named by the kind's or check's name as records and problems carry it. A name the format does not know MUST say so, with a link to the format page.

title: A link stays inside its product
statement: Each product is a space of its own: every link, whatever its relation, MUST join two records of the same product, and the store's link-crosses-product validation refuses one that does not. An ID of another product in text is plain text, never a link.

title: A standard rule is never owed
statement: A `standard_rule` MUST NOT be an obligation: no domain owes it, and coverage MUST NOT count it as designed, built or proved. A `meets` link MUST have no role, so it never counts as design or proof.

title: A standard rule is in use only when something meets it
statement: A standard rule MUST count as in use only when a record links to it with `meets`; naming its ID in text does not meet it. A rule that is not in use has no purpose and MUST be reported.

title: Each step of a technical flow has its own position on its path
statement: The steps on each path of a technical flow MUST each have a different whole-number `position`, numbered 1, 2, 3 without gaps, as a flow's steps are, and a step's path MUST be compared as a flow step's is, main by default.

title: A technical step designs what it satisfies, but only a component builds it
statement: An obligation a technical step `satisfies` MUST count as designed in the step's domain. It MUST count as built only when a component whose file exists satisfies it.

title: A technical flow deepens the flow it carries out
statement: A technical flow SHOULD name the flow it carries out with `deepens`. One that deepens no flow MUST be reported as a warning.

title: An API holds the endpoints of one resource and the rules they share
statement: An API MUST sit directly in a domain and MUST hold only endpoints and interaction requirements, each interaction requirement holding for every endpoint in it. An endpoint MUST sit in an API or directly in its domain.

title: An integration holds one interaction requirement per exchange
statement: An integration MUST sit directly in a domain and MUST hold only interaction requirements, one for each exchange with its outside system. It MAY name that system in `system`.

title: Kinds are read in one order, the schema's
statement: Every list of kinds, in the app, the reference and coverage, MUST read them in one order: Lathe's kinds by their position in the schema (the product and its domains, the Define stage, the Design stage, then open questions), then a product's own kinds by name. No code MAY keep a list of its own.

title: A merge keeps both sides and fails only on a real clash
statement: Merging two branches' data MUST keep the rows each side added, changed or removed, row by row, and MUST fail only on a real clash: one key added on both sides with different content, or one row changed on both sides. A merge MUST NOT bring in a row that breaks its table's own rules.

title: Errors mean broken; warnings mean work to do
statement: A problem MUST be an **error** when the data is broken (the store refuses a row, which is a `data-refused` error, or a check finds what the schema cannot hold, such as a test whose file does not back what it claims) and a **warning** when work is still to do (an obligation not yet satisfied or proved, a use case with no requirements, a component file that does not exist yet).

title: A problem names its check and its record
statement: Every problem MUST name the check that found it and, when it concerns a record, that record's ID. Its message MUST be a plain sentence naming the IDs involved.

title: A check is one row with one query
statement: Each check MUST be a row of the `check` table whose `query` is a single `SELECT` (or `WITH`) statement returning `record` and `message`, and `severity` when the check's severity is `error_or_warning`. Its name MUST be the row's `name`.

title: Checks run in position order
statement: The engine MUST run every check row on every load, in `position` order, and MUST collect the problems of all of them in that order, even when one check fails to run.

title: A structural gap is a warning, not an error
statement: A check that finds two stages not joined up (a rule no use case applies, a use case no flow carries out, an interaction requirement that fulfills nothing, a test whose type does not suit what it proves) MUST report a warning, never an error: it is work still to do, and `lathe check` MUST NOT fail because of it.

title: One mistake gives one error
statement: A row the store refuses MUST be reported once, naming the rule it broke and its file and line, and nothing that only follows from it MAY be reported: refused data is not checked at all until it is fixed. A link to a duplicated ID MUST NOT be refused with the duplicate.

title: A gap check waits until the stage it looks for has started
statement: A check that looks for a missing link to a later stage MUST stay silent in a domain that has no records of that stage yet: `use-case-without-flow` reports nothing in a domain with no flows.

title: A product check keeps the contract of Lathe's checks
statement: A product's own check MUST be a row of the `check` table with the product's `product_id`, kept in the product's `data/check.jsonl` and run exactly as Lathe's checks are: one query over the same tables. Its problems MUST be ordinary problems, reported with Lathe's, and only about records of its product.

title: A product check never shares a name with one of Lathe's checks
statement: Each problem's check name MUST say whether Lathe or the product reported it: a check's name MUST be one key across Lathe's checks and every product's, so the store MUST refuse a product check row named like one of Lathe's checks.

title: Product checks run after Lathe's checks
statement: The engine MUST run every one of Lathe's checks before any product check, so that a product check never changes which of Lathe's problems are found.

title: A product's checks are rows, never a folder
statement: A product MUST add its checks as rows of the `check` table, and `lathe.config.json` MUST refuse a `checks` setting as an unknown setting, so no product names a folder of checks.

title: A step check compares only what it can judge
statement: A flow step check MUST report only the mistake it is for: a step without a whole-number position, two steps in one place and a link to a target that does not exist are refused by the store, and the steps of a flow that carries out no use case are not compared with it.

title: Owed or silent proof is a warning, not an error
statement: Proof still owed, a proof that counts nowhere and a manual test whose file is silent MUST each be reported as a warning, never an error: they are work still to do, and `lathe check` MUST NOT fail because of them.

title: A record holds no more children of one kind than the product allows
statement: A record SHOULD hold at most the product's `max_children` children of any one kind. More than that means a level is missing between them, which is work still to do, not breakage.

title: The children limit is a product setting, 15 by default
statement: The most children of one kind a record should hold MUST be the product's `product_setting.max_children`, and 15 when the product has no `product_setting` row.

title: max_children is a whole number of at least 1
statement: `product_setting.max_children` MUST be a whole number of at least 1, and the store MUST refuse any other value, naming the table.

title: Children are counted per kind
statement: A record's children of different kinds MUST be counted as separate lists, since each kind is shown as its own list.

title: Tests are never counted as one list
statement: Tests MUST NOT be counted toward too many children, because the app groups a domain's tests by what they prove and never shows them as one list.

title: A capability or layer holds more than one record
statement: A capability or a layer SHOULD hold more than one record. One that holds a single record groups nothing, and is work still to do.

title: A lone child is judged on the record's own children of every kind
statement: Whether a capability or layer has a lone child MUST be judged on all its own children, of any kind, and never on its children's children.

title: An empty capability or layer is not a lone child
statement: A capability or layer with no children MUST NOT be reported as having a lone child.

title: Structure size findings are warnings
statement: Too many children and a lone child MUST be warnings, never errors: the spec still loads and checks, and only its shape needs work.

title: A setting a check reads is a typed column of product_setting
statement: Each product setting a check reads MUST be a typed column of the `product_setting` table, with its default when the product has no row, so that Lathe's checks and a product's own checks read the same values.

title: A check row is its own documentation
statement: Every check row MUST give a one-sentence `summary`, an `explanation` ending with how to fix what it reports, and its `severity`. The reference MUST take each check's text from its row and from nowhere else.

title: A check's severity says what its query returns
statement: A check's `severity` MUST be `error` or `warning` when every problem it reports has that severity, and `error_or_warning` exactly when its query returns a `severity` column saying which for each row.

title: Every check that runs is documented, the product's as well as Lathe's
statement: A product's own check rows MUST meet the same rule as Lathe's: the store MUST refuse any check row, Lathe's or a product's, without its summary, explanation, severity or query.

title: A problem's code leads to its check
statement: Wherever a problem's check code is shown, it MUST be a link to that check's page.

title: Every component and test serves an obligation
statement: A component MUST satisfy at least one obligation, and a test MUST prove or support at least one, so that nothing in the design outlives its purpose unseen. One that does not MUST be reported as a warning. No component or test is waived: a component of shared infrastructure links the obligations it makes possible.

title: Every page has its own address
statement: Every page MUST have its own address that can be bookmarked, shared and reloaded, and the browser's back and forward buttons MUST move between pages.

title: A page changes data only through the command layer
statement: A page MUST change a record only when the person acts on one of its record actions (Edit, Add or Remove), and then only by sending one write to `POST /api/write`, which the store's command layer applies or refuses whole. Opening, reading or searching a page MUST NOT send a write, and no page MUST write a data file itself, so every change is one the schema accepts and is reviewed in git.

title: The same graph is always drawn the same way
statement: The same specs MUST always give the same map, and the same focus, depth, filters and mode the same framed picture, so walking the graph is predictable: records in one column keep their order, and their places, whatever is in focus.

title: Filters never hide the focus or reach through hidden records
statement: A graph filter MUST NOT hide the focused record. A record MUST NOT be reached through a hidden kind or a hidden relation: hiding something hides the paths through it too.

title: A group is not a record
statement: A group in the graph MUST be derived from a record and the kind of its children, and MUST NOT appear in the specs: it has no ID of its own, only its parent's ID and the kind, and no record can link to it.

title: Whether a record's children are grouped depends on its children alone
statement: A record's children MUST be grouped exactly when they include more than one kind (a folder only tells kinds apart; LA-EXP-DR27), whatever the focus, depth or filters, so a record always looks the same wherever it is met in the graph.

title: A thing has one address whatever the view
statement: A record MUST have one address, its bare ID (`/<id>`), and a group one address, its place in the graph's tree (`/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>`, or `/<parent-id>/<kind>` for a record's kind group), whichever views (Wiki, Graph, Model) show it; a product's and a domain's address is their overview page. The views MUST NOT change the address's path, only its `view` query parameter, and an older graph address (`/graph/<id>`, or a product's and domain's old graph address) MUST lead to the same thing in the Graph view.

title: Both panes show the same focus
statement: The wiki pane, the graph pane and the side bar MUST always show the same record or group: the one the address names. Moving the center in the graph MUST change the address, and changing the address MUST move every pane.

title: A link's views win over the remembered ones
statement: When an address names views (`?view=wiki`, `?view=wiki,graph`, `?view=graph,model`) the page MUST open with those views, and they become the remembered ones; only an address without views MUST fall back to the views last open. A view the page does not offer (Model, away from a domain, aggregate or entity) MUST be dropped from what it shows; when that leaves none, the page MUST show the wiki.

title: The graph is a view of a page, not a place in the nav
statement: The graph MUST be reached as a view of the page in hand (its Graph view toggle, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+2, the command palette), never as a separate item in the side navigation.

title: The current space is the page's product
statement: The current space MUST be the product of the page on screen when it belongs to one (its product, domain, record or group page, or its Checks page); on a page outside every space (the products, the format, Settings) it MUST stay the space last chosen, or the first product.

title: A space's icon is its own or its monogram
statement: A product's icon MUST be its `icon` field when that is one emoji or up to two characters, and otherwise its ID as a monogram. Its color MUST be its `color` field when that is a hex color or a color name, and otherwise one derived from its ID, the same on every visit.

title: Spaces keep the products' order
statement: Spaces MUST be in the products' ID order everywhere they are listed, and the nth space MUST be the one Alt+n opens.

title: A space's last page lasts the session
statement: The last page visited in each space MUST be remembered for the browser session only, never across sessions.

title: A space shows only its own product
statement: Every view and count inside a space MUST show only its own product's records, links, coverage and problems, and those that belong to no product: never a record, link or problem of another product, nor a link to one from an ID named in text. Another product MUST stay one choice away in the rail.

title: Siblings share a column
statement: In the graph, every record or group with the same parent MUST sit in the same column, whatever its kind, so no sibling is further left or further right than another. A column is a depth in the parent/child tree around the focus; within a column, siblings MUST stay together, ordered by their parent's place, then by kind, then by ID.

title: Folder names and order come from the workspace
statement: The app MUST take the folders' names and order from `Workspace.sections` and each kind's folder from its `section`, never from its own code. A stage's name is its own, capitalized.

title: The nav and the pages read one folder model
statement: The side nav, the domain page and the group pages MUST place records in folders by the same model, so they name and order folders alike.

title: A record's folder comes from its kind
statement: A record MUST be shown in its kind's folder, wherever its file lives; a kind in no listed folder MUST be shown in a folder of its own, at the end of its stage or, with no stage, after the stages.

title: A record below a listed one is reached through it
statement: A record that no folder lists, such as a requirement under its use case, MUST be reached through the listed record above it, whose branch opens for it.

title: What is folded in the nav lasts for the session
statement: Which nav rows are open MUST be remembered for the session only, never across sessions.

title: A layer is a record, a test group is not
statement: A group that is a record (a layer, a capability, a use case) MUST link to its page wherever it heads its members; a group computed by the app (a test group) MUST NOT pose as a record: its nav row only folds and its heading is not a link.

title: Test groups are computed by one model, never stored
statement: A test's group MUST be computed from its `proves` links each time the specs load, never stored in a record, and the side nav, the pages and the graph MUST take it from the same folder model, so they never disagree.

title: A test sits in one group, by its family first
statement: A test MUST sit in exactly one test group, judged by its family first: Acceptance tests when it sits under a capability or proves a UC requirement; UI tests or Design checks when its `test_type` is `ui` or `design`; then Domain rule tests, Pattern tests, UI tests (proving an interaction requirement at a view), Interaction tests, Design checks (its links are all `supports`) and Engineering checks, by the first that applies to what it proves. The groups are shown in the order acceptance, domain rule, pattern, interaction, UI, design, engineering; within a group, tests sit by their capability, then the first use case or pattern they prove, in ID order.

title: Ordered groups come in their order, what is outside any comes last
statement: Layers and capabilities MUST be listed by their `position`, then by ID, never by ID alone; the records outside any of them MUST come after them.

title: A split appears only when there is more than one to tell apart
statement: A list MUST be split by kind, or by a computed group such as a test group, only when it holds more than one kind or group to tell apart; with one, its records MUST be listed directly, with no level, heading, row, tag or graph folder for the one kind or group. Groups that are records (layers, capabilities, use cases, patterns) and the fixed stages and folders are not such splits and stay.

title: An empty test group is never shown
statement: A test group with no tests MUST NOT be shown in the nav, on a page or in the graph.

title: Group labels are plain English and name kinds through plural()
statement: A group's label MUST read as plain English, and any kind it names MUST come from the workspace's kind labels through `plural()`, such as "Components outside any layer", so a product that renames a kind sees its own name.

title: Motion carries no meaning and is turned off under reduced motion
statement: Motion in the graph MUST only help the eye follow a change: the view after a move MUST be the same with or without it, and when the system asks for reduced motion the camera MUST jump to the new view with no glide.

title: One tab per page at most, and one preview tab at most
statement: A tab group MUST NOT hold two tabs for one page, nor more than one preview tab. Opening a page already open activates its tab; a plain open of another page replaces the preview tab's page, keeping its place in the row.

title: There is always a tab
statement: A tab group showing a page MUST hold at least one tab, the page's. Closing its last tab MUST leave that page open, as the preview tab.

title: A tab's state is its own
statement: Changing the views, pane sizes, scroll or graph settings of the active tab MUST NOT change any other tab's. A new tab copies the active tab's state when it opens, then goes its own way.

title: The address names the active tab
statement: The address MUST name the active tab's page and, once its views are named, its views: activating, cycling or closing a tab moves the address, and a link to a page open in another tab shows that tab as it was and rewrites the address to its views. Back to a page whose tab was closed reopens it as the preview tab.

title: A list of one kind is titled by that kind
statement: A list of a record's children or a group's members MUST be titled by its kind's plural label, through `plural()`, when it holds one kind ("Domain rules", "UC requirements", "Components"), and MUST be titled "Children" or "Members" only when it holds more than one kind to tell apart. Its count stays beside the title, and its accessible name and search box follow the title ("Domain rules of LA-EXP-A1", "Filter domain rules").

title: An ERD draws exactly one line per relationship link
statement: An aggregate's ERD MUST draw exactly one line for each `has_one`, `has_many` and `refers_to` link its entities hold, so each such link of a domain appears in exactly one aggregate's ERD. A domain's ERD MUST draw exactly one line for each aggregate pair and direction that a `refers_to` link between their entities joins, and no line that no link stands for.

title: A box from another domain is gray and names its owner
statement: In an ERD a box owned by the current domain MUST be blue, and a box owned by another domain MUST be gray and labeled with its owner in parentheses: its domain for an aggregate, its domain and aggregate for an entity. A box from another aggregate of the same domain stays blue and names its aggregate.

title: A selected row is the whole row
statement: In the nav, as in VS Code's explorer, a row MUST be as wide as the nav panel, indented by padding for its depth rather than by nested margins, with its indent guides and its fold chevron inside it. The current page's row MUST carry the selection over the whole row, from the panel's left edge over the indent and the chevron to its right edge, in the selection tint with its text and chevron in steel, with no bar of its own at its edge. A hovered row MUST take the hover tint over the whole row, and while the nav is used from the keyboard the selected and the focused row MUST show a 1 px steel outline. The lists stay nested for screen readers.

title: By touch, a tap selects a node and a second tap opens it
statement: A finger has no hover, so on a canvas a first tap on a node MUST select it and say what it is before anything moves, and only a second tap on the same node, or an explicit Open, MUST open it. A pointer that can hover opens a node with one click.

title: A canvas stays mounted and is fitted before it paints
statement: The graph and the Model view MUST keep their canvas mounted while their content changes, MUST fit their first picture before it paints, and MUST NOT cut a glide short by fitting again when their size has not changed.

title: A product and a domain have one page, at their ID
statement: A product's and a domain's only page MUST be their overview, at their bare ID (`/LA`, `/LA-EXP`); there MUST NOT be a second, generic record page for them. That one page MUST lose nothing the generic page showed: its text in the wiki, and in the side bar its kind, fields, data file, parent, children, links out and in, and problems.

title: The graph's tree is the nav's tree
statement: The graph MUST walk the same tree the nav shows, from the one folder model: a domain holds its stages (Define, Design) and the folders outside every stage, a stage its folders, a folder its records, and a product its Shared folder, then its domains, then its open questions. A folder that mixes kinds the nav lists side by side (Interaction design: flows, views, endpoints) MUST split into one group per kind; a folder of one kind, or one that lists containers and then the records outside any (Capabilities; Technical specification), MUST NOT. Empty stages and folders are not drawn. Every stage, folder and group MUST be a node with its own address (`/<domain-id>/define`, `/<domain-id>/design/technical-specification`), labeled and counted as in the nav.

title: Depth counts the levels the camera frames below the focus
statement: Depth N MUST frame the focus, its parent at the left edge for context, and its descendants down to N levels below it, every stage, folder and group counting as a level, as in a file explorer. Depth MUST NOT add siblings or ancestors further up to the picture it frames, though the map around it stays in view. Depth stays 1 to 3, and a group at the center counts levels the same way. The side bar's lists and the summary count this framed picture.

title: The Model view's camera frames its boxes in focus only
statement: The Model view's camera, framing a new picture and on the Fit command, MUST fit the bounding box of its boxes in focus only, so its context ring (`LA-EXP-UC11-R06`) may run past the canvas's edges; a soft vignette of the canvas's own background at its edges MUST make the cut-off read as meant.

title: Links adds the center's own links, one hop
statement: With the Links switch on, the graph MUST add the records the focused record links to and from, one hop, with the relation filters applied, and the links between them and the focus, drawn as dashed curves in their own color (`--link-edge`) between their boxes. Each linked record is drawn wherever it sits in the map, whatever its size on screen, and keeps its own place there: links never move anything. A linked record off screen MUST be counted by the edge hint on its side (`LA-EXP-UC03-R12`). With it off, the graph MUST draw no cross-links. Trace mode stays for a whole chain.

title: A domain's ERD draws one "reacts to" line per aggregate pair and event
statement: A domain's ERD MUST draw exactly one dashed "reacts to" line for each `reacts_to` link from an aggregate to an event that another aggregate raises, when either aggregate is in the domain, running from the raising aggregate to the reacting one. An aggregate reacting to its own event, and a use case or component reacting to an event, MUST NOT draw a line there.

title: Domain events are drawn in the spark colors
statement: Wherever a domain event is drawn as a node or box (the ERD, the graph), it MUST be a flag, notched on the right (`LA-EXP-DR65`), in the `--spark` and `--spark-bg` tokens, and its `raised_by` and `reacts_to` lines MUST be drawn in `--spark`, the `reacts_to` lines dashed, so events read the same in every view.

title: The side bar never repeats what the page shows
statement: What the side bar shows MUST earn its place: no list or fact the main view already shows beside it (a record's children, its problems, its links grouped by label in the wiki's Traceability). It describes what the main view does not: the node under the pointer or selected, the file behind the page, the page's outline, and the file's history.

title: A record's history is read from git, never written
statement: A record's history MUST come from git's own log of the record's rows in its table's data file, the file found from the data by the record's ID, never from a path a request names. Reading it MUST change nothing: no commit, no lock, no change to the git config, and no command built from text a shell reads.

title: The graph is one fixed map of its product's tree
statement: Each product MUST have a graph of its own: its tree laid out once per load of the specs, as one icicle with the product as its single root, then its Shared folder, domains, stages, folders and records and their children, as the nav's tree has them (`LA-EXP-DR45`). No node, link, hint or minimap box of another product MAY be in it; a record no product reaches is the root of a map of its own. A node's size MUST come from the tree alone, top-down from the product's fixed box (`LA-EXP-DR58`), never from what is in focus: the product's box is as wide as it is tall; a parent's children split its height equally, a gap apart of a tenth of each one's part, their stack filling it from its top edge to its bottom edge, in the tree's order; and every box in one depth column has the same width, each column 0.4 times as wide as the one before, with a gap before it of 0.15 times its width, so the column widths are fixed fractions of the map. Each label is centered in its box. Each parent line MUST be drawn level, at the child's middle, from the parent's outline to the child's. Nothing in the map is ever laid out again or resized while the person walks it; filters hide nodes without moving the rest. A trace is a chain, not a tree, and keeps a small picture of its own, in columns of 190 by 56 boxes at text scale 1, each as tall as its wrapped label if taller.

title: Siblings are the same size, with the same text
statement:
One rule MUST size every layout of the graph (Tree, Nested and Voronoi), top-down from one fixed product box: siblings are the same size, with the same text. The product's box MUST have a fixed size, the same for every product (300,000 map units), and each parent MUST split its room equally among its children, in the tree's order. Record counts and titles MUST size no box: a busy sibling packs its children smaller, and a quiet one has blank space. How each layout splits its room is `LA-EXP-DR57` (Tree), `LA-EXP-DR62` (Nested) and `LA-EXP-DR64` (Voronoi).

A node's label is part of the map. A box's text scale MUST be at most a fixed share of its box's size, the same share at every depth: its size over 400 map units, its size being its column's width in the Tree (where siblings split their parent's height), its side in Nested and the square root of its area in Voronoi. Siblings MUST share one text scale: the largest, at most that share, at which every sibling's whole label fits its room, its kind and ID line and its title wrapped on whole words, with its padding, its marks, its shape's room and its border. So a framed box's header reads at about the same size on screen whichever box is framed, and very small boxes have very small text, read by zooming in. Its title, its kind and ID line, its padding and its problem badge MUST grow by that scale, in map units, whatever the person's text size; its border, outline and parent line's stroke grow with it too (never below half in the Nested and Voronoi views), so a box's edge stays in proportion to its label; a trace's boxes are at text scale 1. The text MUST never change size relative to its box: not when the focus changes, not when the camera zooms or settles; only the camera changes how big it looks. Every drawn box shows its label at that size, however small it is on screen (`LA-EXP-DR60`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`).

A title MUST wrap on whole words, after a space, never cut off or ended with an ellipsis; only a word too wide for a line on its own MAY break, after a hyphen (or a slash in a file's path) first, and the text scale never lets that happen in a map. The kind and ID line MAY wrap too. Lines MUST be broken when the map is built, measured by the canvas's own text metrics in the label's faces once they have loaded (the theme's body and mono faces), and the canvas MUST draw exactly those lines in those faces, so the map is laid out once per spec load and its faces, and is the same every time for a given face. Each line's height MUST be in proportion to its text, so no glyph is clipped. Map units MUST be kept in doubles, never rounded, so the deepest boxes keep their places however small they are against the product's box.

title: Focusing moves the camera, never the map
statement:
Focusing a node, by a click, the address, Back and Forward, the step keys or the trail, MUST move the camera only: it MUST frame the focus and the levels the depth shows below it to fill the pane, with the parent's level kept in view in a strip at the left edge. The camera's zoom limits MUST let it frame the deepest leaf of a large product, which is very small against the product's box (`LA-EXP-DR58`), and fit the whole map in a phone's pane: 64 times the map's units at most, a ten-thousandth at least. The framed levels MUST fit the pane, however small their labels then are on screen; the depth decides only what is framed. The camera MUST move there from the view as it is, including one the person zoomed or panned, in one smooth zoom and pan (zooming out only as far as the pan needs) on the shared motion (`--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease`, at most twice the speed for a long path); on a page's first picture, on a resize and under reduced motion it MUST go there at once. Free zoom and pan move the same camera: the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer, a drag pans, and the zoom buttons zoom about the pane's middle; a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and the frame button and the `.` command frame the focus again.

The map MUST be drawn on a canvas, anew for each frame of the camera. A viewport MUST be kept in doubles, and every map point placed on screen in doubles relative to the camera's center, with no transform but the screen's pixel ratio, so a box deep in a large map is as steady at a deep zoom as at the top. Each label's lines MUST be drawn at their size in the map times the zoom, so text is crisp at any zoom whatever the map's range. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, MUST carry focus, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, and each box's role and name for assistive technology, and the box it focuses is drawn with the focus ring. The pointer MUST find the box under it from the map's own outlines (a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners, a Voronoi cell's polygon), the last drawn first, so a child drawn over its parent is found before it.

title: The graph draws only what is in view and big enough to see
statement: The graph MUST draw only the nodes in view (with a tenth of the pane to spare each way) and at least 3 pixels tall on screen. Every drawn node MUST show its label, its kind and ID line and its full title wrapped on whole words, at its fixed size in the map (`LA-EXP-DR58`), however small it is on screen (small text is read by zooming in): whether a node is drawn never depends on whether its text can be read, and the focus and the depth decide only what the camera frames (`LA-EXP-DR59`). Each frame the canvas MUST draw each drawn node's shape, border and fill, and its label's lines at their map size times the zoom; a line under 2 pixels on screen MAY be drawn as a faint bar where its glyphs would be, which still shows the label. A drawn node's children too small to draw MUST be one bar in their level for each run of them. Level by level from the roots, a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes MUST be drawn as one bar per parent instead, so a product of thousands of records stays within the performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`). The keyboard's layer of drawn boxes (`LA-EXP-DR59`) MUST take what a glide passes over once, as it starts, and be trimmed when it ends, so no frame of the glide rebuilds it.

title: A domain is drawn as a hexagon
statement: In the graph every domain node MUST be drawn as a hexagon, with flat top and bottom edges and pointed left and right ends, drawn as a polygon, not a rotated box. The points' chamfer MUST grow with the node's box scale (12 map units at box scale 1), at most a quarter of its width, so a very tall domain still reads as a hexagon and not as a diamond. Its border MUST follow the outline in every state, hovered, focused, keyboard-focused and selected by a tap, by coloring and thickening the outline's own edge, drawn inside the polygon. A parent line into a domain MUST meet the tip of its point, and a parent line out of one MUST start on its slanted side, where the outline is at the child's middle; a line meets every other shape's outline the same way (`LA-EXP-DR65`). The minimap draws boxes.

title: The Nested map holds each box's children inside it, every box a square
statement:
In the Nested view the graph MUST lay out the same tree as the Tree view (`LA-EXP-DR45`), its product's alone with the product as its single root and nothing of another product, once per load of the specs, as nested squares, top-down from the product's fixed square by `LA-EXP-DR58`'s rule: siblings are the same size, with the same text. A parent's room under its header band, inside its padding, MUST hold its children as a grid of equal squares in the tree's order, row by row, a gap apart, with the column count that makes the squares largest; room the grid leaves is blank. The padding and the gaps are shares of the box's side (8 and 6 at its side's text scale), so the layout is the same at any size. Siblings share one text scale, their side over 400 map units or the largest below it at which every sibling's whole label fits: a leaf's centered in its square, a parent's in a header band at most a quarter of its square. Siblings share one header band too, as tall as the tallest of their labels at that scale. Record counts size nothing.

A box with children MUST show its label in its header band at its top and hold its children below it, so no two siblings overlap and no child leaves its parent. A label's kind and ID line and its title each wrap on whole words, never inside one, and nothing is clipped: a leaf's label is centered in it, a parent's sits at the top left of its header band. Every drawn box shows its label (`LA-EXP-DR60`). A domain is a square there, with a small hexagon mark in its header (`LA-EXP-DR61` holds in the Tree view). The focus never changes the map, and filters hide boxes without moving the rest. No parent lines are drawn: holding is the parent link.

title: Nested: the camera frames the focus box, depth labels inside it
statement: In the Nested view, focusing a node by any of the ways `LA-EXP-DR59` lists MUST move the same camera, in the same glide, to frame the focus's box in the pane, within the padding and centered, within the camera's zoom limits (`LA-EXP-DR59`). The Nested camera frames the focus's box whatever the depth, so the depth control is off in the Nested view. The level of detail is `LA-EXP-DR60`'s: only boxes in view and at least 3 pixels on screen each way are drawn, each with its label, a parent before its children so a child is drawn over its parent, and a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes is not drawn (its parents stand for it). The keyboard's order is the tree's, a parent before its children. With Links on, the focus's links MUST be drawn as curves between the drawn boxes, and edge hints point to those out of view.

title: The Voronoi map splits each cell into its children's cells
statement:
In the Voronoi view the graph MUST lay out the same tree as the Tree view (`LA-EXP-DR45`), its product's alone with the product as its single root, once per load of the specs, as a Voronoi treemap, top-down from the product's fixed hexagon by `LA-EXP-DR58`'s rule: siblings are the same size, with the same text. The product is a flat-topped regular hexagon as wide as the other layouts' product box, and each cell with children MUST be split into equal-area cells for them, each within about 5% of the others, by a Voronoi diagram (a power diagram) clipped to the cell's outline inside a padding and below its header, its children a gap apart, every cell convex. The diagram is iterated until the area error is under 0.2% of the parent's area. Record counts size nothing. The layout MUST be deterministic: a parent's children start evenly round a circle about its largest inscribed point, in the tree's order clockwise from the upper left, each nudged by its ID, with a random number generator seeded by their IDs, and each parent is laid out in its own frame, so the same tree always gives the same picture, and adding one record moves nothing outside its parent's cell.

Siblings MUST share one text scale: their size (the square root of a cell's area) over 400 map units, or the largest below it at which every sibling's label fits its room, the smallest sibling cell's room deciding. A leaf's label is centered on its largest inscribed point, as wide as the cell allows there, and a parent's sits in a header at the top of its cell, its children below the header's cut, which leaves them at least 55% of the cell. A label wraps on whole words and is never clipped, so every cell shows its name (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`). A domain is a cell there, with the hexagon mark before its kind and ID line. The focus never changes the map, filters hide cells without moving the rest, and no parent lines are drawn: holding is the parent link. The layout MUST run in a web worker where there is one, and a spec loaded again with the same tree and labels MUST reuse the map it had.

title: Each kind is drawn in a shape of its own
statement:
In the graph every kind MUST have one shape, the same in every view, as a secondary cue after its label, and every shape MUST keep a rectangular footprint so boxes still stack:

| Group | Kind | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | product | a large rounded box |
| | domain | a hexagon (`LA-EXP-DR61`) |
| | stage and folder groups | a folder with a tab |
| | capability | a slice pointing right |
| Define | aggregate | a double border |
| | entity | a plain box |
| | domain rule, pattern rule | an octagon |
| | domain event | a flag, notched on the right |
| | use case | a stadium |
| | requirement | a page with a folded corner; an interaction requirement too, with a marker |
| | pattern | stacked boxes |
| Design | flow | a chevron bar |
| | flow step, technical step | a chevron |
| | view | a window with a top bar |
| | endpoint | a box with a port notch on its left |
| | API, integration | a plain box with a port mark |
| | layer | a striped box |
| | component | a box with component tabs |
| | test | a shield |
| | technical flow | as a flow, with a gear mark |
| Other | open question | a diamond |
| | standard, standard rule | as a pattern and a pattern rule, with a ruler mark |

A kind a product adds MUST be a plain box. In the Tree view and a trace a box's outline MUST be its kind's shape: a polygon shape drawn with its edge inside the polygon, so its border, hover, focus, keyboard ring and a tap's selection color and thicken the outline itself, and a rounded shape with its border's corners and its rings following them. In the Nested and Voronoi views every box MUST keep its rectangle or cell and show its kind's shape as a small mark before its kind and ID line. A shape's corners and notches MUST grow with its box's scale, at most a share of its side. Its label and problem badge MUST stay inside its shape's safe area, which the map keeps when it wraps and sizes the label, so no line is clipped or crowded by a notch or a corner. The Model view MUST draw a domain event as the same flag, and every shape and mark MUST be in the graph's key (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R21`).

title: A record form offers only what the schema allows
statement: A record's form MUST be generated from the schema description, never written per kind: one input per column of the kind's table but its ID and parent columns, typed by the column (an enum a select, a whole number a number input, true or false a check, a date a date input, a list one entry per item), its required columns marked; its parent chosen among the records of the kind's allowed parent kinds in the same product; each link's targets among the records of the kinds its relation allows, in the same product; and its part rows with their own columns. A kind a product declares MUST get its form the same way.

title: A refused change shows its reasons in place and changes nothing
statement: When the store refuses a write, the form or question MUST stay open with what the person entered, show every reason the store gave beside the input or section its command came from, and take focus to the reasons. Nothing on the page, and no data file, MUST change.

title: The workspace is rebuilt from the data files on every load
statement: Each load MUST read the data files afresh, Lathe's own check rows beside the product's, into a new in-memory DuckDB through the store. The engine MUST NOT write a database file or keep the data between loads, so the data files stay the only source of truth. It MAY keep the reference while no file in the data folders or the schema has changed.

title: A load stays within the engine's performance budgets
statement: Loading Lathe's own spec (about 1,800 records, every data file read and loaded with every key and rule, then checked) MUST take under 2 s, and a live reload after one row changes under 500 ms, on the dev machine, as `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf` measures (`lathe/perf/engine.ts`, which also measures a synthetic product of about 10,000 records and the reference without a budget). The checks and the coverage queries run side by side on a few connections to the same database; every check still runs on every load, because a check reads across kinds (a link's target, a parent chain, coverage), so a change to one row can change the problems of records of other kinds. When the machine is busy (a one-minute load average above 12) the script measures but judges nothing; a budget is never loosened to make a busy run pass.

title: Hiding a panel gives its space away and loses nothing
statement: Hiding the nav or the side bar MUST give its space to the main view and MUST keep a control that brings it back: the nav keeps its rail, and the side bar's toggle sits in the page panel's top-right corner, as VS Code's layout toggles do, never as a full-height strip. The side bar MUST describe the same page whichever view is open, so hiding a pane never hides the record's facts for good.

title: A key binding means one command wherever it applies
statement: No two commands MUST share a binding in contexts that can be active at the same time, and no two-key sequence MUST start with a key that is a binding of its own.

title: Typing is never taken as a shortcut
statement: A shortcut without Ctrl, Cmd or Alt (a letter, a symbol, a sequence such as `g c`) MUST NOT fire while focus is in a text input, a text area, a select or editable text.

title: The browser's essential keys stay the browser's
statement: No binding, default or overridden, MUST take Cmd/Ctrl+W, T, L, R, N or Q, Tab, F5 or F11, and the app MUST call preventDefault only for keys it handles, so Alt+Left and Alt+Right still go back and forward.

title: Every hint reads from the keymap
statement: Every shortcut hint (tooltip, palette row, sheet row, `aria-keyshortcuts`, placeholder) MUST be read from the one keymap with the person's overrides applied, so a rebinding changes every hint; no hint is written by hand.

title: Keys are shown as the platform shows them
statement: Keys MUST be shown as the platform shows them: on a Mac as the symbols ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ in Apple's order ("⇧⌘P"), elsewhere as words joined by + ("Ctrl+Shift+P").

title: aria-keyshortcuts names only whole chords
statement: `aria-keyshortcuts` MUST name each single-chord binding with the DOM's modifier names ("Control+Shift+P"), and MUST leave out a sequence ("g then c"), which it cannot express.

title: A tooltip never gets in the way
statement: At most one tooltip MUST show at a time; a click or a page moving focus on load MUST NOT open one; Escape, leaving the control or moving focus away MUST close it.

title: A theme sets tokens and nothing else
statement: A theme MUST be data: token names from the app's token table, each with a value of its kind. It MUST NOT carry selectors, rules or any text beyond those values.

title: Every theme has a light set and a dark set
statement: Every theme MUST set the core colors (shell, paper, sheet, ink, muted, rule, the accent and its tint, spark and its tint, and warning) in both its light and dark sets. The other colors follow a core one (the graph's stages follow the accent, errors follow spark) or serve both modes, unless the theme sets them.

title: A theme file says its format and version and holds known tokens only
statement: A theme file MUST be JSON with `format` "lathe-theme", `version` 1, a `name` of 1 to 60 characters, and `light`, `dark` and `tokens` objects. A file with any other field, an unknown token, or a value that is not exactly a value of its kind MUST be refused with a message saying why. Core colors a file leaves out MUST be taken from Lathe.

title: Built-in themes are never changed
statement: A built-in theme MUST NOT be edited, renamed or deleted; it is changed by editing a copy. Reset MUST put a copy back to the built-in it was copied from, keeping its name.

title: A theme that is gone falls back to Lathe
statement: When the chosen theme no longer exists (deleted, or its stored data no longer reads), Lathe MUST be shown and chosen.

title: A phone shows one view of a page at a time
statement: On a screen too narrow for panes side by side, a page MUST show exactly one of its views, the first of those its address names, and the address MUST name the view shown. The views a page has open on a wide screen are not lost by reading it on a phone.

title: A sheet keeps focus until it closes, then gives it back
statement: A sheet (the nav, the side bar, the open pages, quick find) MUST take focus as it opens, keep Tab and Shift+Tab inside it while it is open, close with Escape, and give focus back to the control that opened it.

title: The frame of a page holds still
statement: The nav, the pane bars, the pane titles, the canvases and the side bar MUST keep their place and size unless the Reader moves or resizes them; a change of page changes what they show, not where they are. Content that arrives after the page is drawn (the specs, the fonts, what the graph tells the side bar) MUST take room kept for it, arrive before paint, or be drawn where it pushes nothing the Reader can see.

title: A bar keeps one height, and a scroll box its gutter
statement: A bar above content that must not move (a pane title above a canvas, the graph's trail and toolbar, the Model view's caption and key) MUST have a fixed block size, or be one line cut with an ellipsis whose whole text is its tooltip, and text that changes in it MUST be one text, so a new number never moves what follows. A box that scrolls up and down MUST keep room for its scrollbar (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`), so its content keeps its width when the scrollbar comes and goes.

title: A standalone action is a button; a link is navigation in context
statement: A control that stands on its own and does something, or takes the Reader somewhere as a step of its own (opening a product's overview, clearing the graph's filters, expanding every row, cancelling a form), MUST look like a button: a ghost button, or the primary button for the one main action of a form. A link MUST look like a link only where it is navigation in context: inside a sentence or Markdown, in a list or a row, in a breadcrumb or trail, and in the navigation. An action that goes to an address MUST still be a real link, so it can be opened in a new tab.

title: A control's name holds its visible text
statement: A control's accessible name MUST contain the text it shows, so a person who says what they see, or hears the name read, finds the same control. Where a control shows a count or a mark, the name is built from what is shown, with words for a screen reader added beside it in hidden text (`sr-only`), rather than an `aria-label` that says something else: the nav's Checks row is named "Checks 3 errors 12 warnings", and a space's button, which shows a monogram the reader is not meant to hear, is named by its product's title in hidden text, with the mark hidden. An `aria-label` that stays MUST include the shown text as a word: "Open pages: 2".

title: No control inside another
statement: A control MUST NOT hold another control: a screen reader reads the outer one as one thing and cannot reach the inner one. Where two act on one item, they sit side by side in a plain wrapper, as a page tab and its close button do.

title: A box that scrolls can be reached by keyboard
statement: A box that scrolls on its own and holds nothing that takes focus (a code block, the ERD's key, the shortcuts sheet's groups) MUST take focus itself (`tabindex="0"`) and be named as a region, so the arrow keys can scroll it.

title: A target is at least 24 px, or has room around it
statement: On any pointer, a link or control that is not inside a sentence MUST be at least 24 by 24 px, or stand far enough from its neighbors that a 24 px circle on it touches no other target (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8). Record links listed in a table cell or the side bar are drawn one line tall at 24 px. On a coarse pointer the larger 44 px of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07` applies.

title: Text sits only on the surfaces the theme vouches for
statement: Body text and muted text MUST be drawn only on the surfaces whose contrast every built-in theme guarantees: the page (`--paper`) and a sheet (`--sheet`), which the theme contrast audit (`app/src/theme/audit.ts`) holds to 4.5:1 in light and dark. The shell (`--shell`) is the gap between panels and holds no text: a page that is one panel, such as Checks or Appearance, draws its own `--paper` background rather than let the shell show through.

title: A folder opens only when it holds lathe.config.json or a data folder
statement: A folder MUST open only when it holds a `lathe.config.json` that is valid JSON (whose `data` names the data folder, `data` by default), or else a `data/` folder. Any other folder MUST be refused with a message that says what is missing, and no window opens.

title: Each folder has one window
statement: Opening a folder that already has a window MUST bring that window forward instead of opening a second one.

title: A window reopens where it was left, on a screen
statement: Each folder's window size, position, and whether it was maximized or full screen MUST be saved when it moves, resizes or closes, and its next window MUST open with them. A saved place that is no longer on a connected screen MUST give way to a centered window, and a size larger than the largest screen MUST shrink to fit it.

title: The page reaches the shell only through window.latheDesktop
statement: Every window MUST run its page with context isolation and the sandbox on and Node integration off. The preload MUST expose only `window.latheDesktop` with `isDesktop`, `platform`, `onCommand` and `setChrome`, and nothing of Node or Electron.

title: Links that leave the app open in the system browser
statement: A link to any other origin than the window's own server MUST open in the system browser, and the window MUST NOT navigate away from Lathe or open windows of its own.

title: Recent folders are listed latest first, each once, at most 10
statement: The recent folders MUST list the folder opened last first, each folder once (opening one again moves it to the top), and at most 10, dropping the oldest.

title: The last folder opened reopens on launch
statement: On launch the shell MUST open a folder named on its command line or dropped on its Dock icon; else the most recent folder that still opens; else, run from Lathe's own repo, that repo; else it MUST ask for a folder.

title: The shell never starts anything on port 5199
statement: Every server the shell starts MUST listen on a free local port other than 5199, which is the owner's own dev server. The shell MAY connect to 5199, and only when it answers.

title: The 5199 dev server is shared only for the folder it reads
statement: In development a window MUST load `http://localhost:5199` only when it answers `GET /api/spec` and names the opened folder as its product folder in `x-lathe-root` (a server without the header is taken to read the repo the shell runs from). Otherwise the window MUST get a dev server of its own.

title: A window's server stops with it
statement: A server the shell started for a window MUST stop when that window closes or the shell quits, including when it is stopped from a terminal.

title: The window's chrome takes only colors the shell has checked
statement: The main process MUST accept a page's chrome only as exactly `{ background, foreground }`, each an opaque hex color (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`), and only from the window's own page. It MUST ignore anything else and leave the window as it was.

title: The Dock badge follows the window in front
statement: The badge MUST show the error count of the focused product window, or of the one focused last while another app is in front. A count MUST be a whole number from 0 up, from the window's own page; anything else MUST be ignored.

title: A record action names only a record ID, and the shell finds its data file
statement: The main process MUST accept a record action only as exactly `{ action, id }`, a known action and an ID in the record ID format, from a product window's own page. It MUST find the data file that holds the record's row itself, among the folder's data files, and MUST NOT open, reveal or run anything a page names as a path.

title: A launch, error or About page runs only the buttons it shows
statement: A button press from the shell's own pages MUST run only when it is one of the actions that page shows, and only from that page.

title: macOS keeps no window state for Lathe
statement: The app MUST opt out of macOS window restoration (`ApplePersistenceIgnoreState`, `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows`), since it reopens its own windows, so a run that was killed leaves macOS nothing to offer to reopen.

title: A write is all or nothing
statement: A write's commands MUST all take effect or none: when one is refused, the data and every data file MUST stay as they were before the write.

title: A write is checked whole before any file changes
statement: Each write MUST build the new state in one transaction, with every key, constraint and validation query of the schema (a link's pair, a link across products, an aggregate's one root, a product kind's product), and MUST rewrite a data file only after the whole state passes.

title: A write rewrites only its tables' files, in one fixed form
statement: A write MUST rewrite only the data files of the tables it changed, each through a temporary file and a rename, with its rows sorted by key and its columns in the table's order, so the same data always gives the same file and a changed row is a one-line diff.

title: Writes run one after another
statement: Writes to one store MUST run one at a time, each on the state the one before it left, so two writers never lose each other's change.

title: A refusal names every problem and where it is
statement: A refused write or load MUST name every problem it found, each with its rule, a message naming the table, row and value, and the data file and line of a loaded row or the index of the command that brought it.

title: A record changes parent only by a move, which carries what sits inside
statement: `set` MUST NOT change a row's key or a record's parent columns. `move` MUST give the record its new parent's column and fill the other parent columns it needs from the new parent's ancestry, and the records inside it MUST keep their parents and take the new derived columns.

title: A removal takes its parts and links, and is refused while referenced
statement: Removing a record MUST take its part rows and the links it starts with it, and MUST be refused, naming up to 20 referrers, while anything else still references it: a child, a link to it, or another record's row naming it.

title: Designed, built and proved are counted only from links
statement: An obligation (a record of a kind marked as an obligation) MUST count as **satisfied** (designed) only when at least one link whose relation has the `design` role targets it, as **built** only when at least one such link comes from a component whose `file` exists, and as **proved** only when at least one link with the `proof` role comes from an automated or manual test. A component whose file does not exist yet still counts as designed, never as built, and a planned test counts as planned, never as proof. Coverage MUST be counted in the domain the obligation belongs to, wherever the component or test sits.

title: Only automated and manual tests prove
statement: A proof link MUST count as proof only when its source's `state` is `automated` or `manual`. A planned test MUST NOT count as proof, and every test gives its state.

title: Built needs a component whose file exists
statement: An obligation MUST count as built only when a design link from a component whose `file` exists targets it. An obligation designed only by another kind, such as a technical step or a product's own design kind, is designed but not built.

title: A file names an ID only as a whole ID
