statement: When the engine looks for an ID in a file a record names, it MUST match the ID only as a whole ID: `TL-LEND-DR05` MUST NOT be found in the text `name TL-LEND-DR050` or `name TL-LEND-DR05-R01`. Otherwise a test could seem to prove a rule its file never names.

title: A use case that follows a pattern gives every one of the pattern's settings
statement: A use case that follows a pattern MUST give each of the pattern's settings a `setting_value` row for that pattern and setting, with a value or with a not-applicable reason. The pattern's rules then apply to the use case with those values, and the use case does not restate them.

title: Each followed pattern's settings take their own values
statement: A use case that follows two patterns with a setting of the same name MUST give each pattern its own value, since a `setting_value` row names its pattern; one pattern's value MUST NOT answer the other's.

title: A pattern rule is owed by the domains that follow its pattern
statement: A pattern rule belongs to no domain. Each domain that follows the pattern, itself or through its use cases, MUST owe the rule as one of its own obligations, and a domain that does not follow the pattern MUST NOT owe it.

title: Each domain designs and proves a pattern rule for itself
statement: A component or test MUST count toward a pattern rule only in the domain it sits in. One domain's proof of a shared rule MUST NOT count as proof for another domain, since each applies the rule with its own setting values.

title: A pattern rule is Not applicable only when every following use case says so
statement: A domain MUST NOT owe a pattern rule when the rule depends on a setting, the domain itself does not follow the pattern, and every one of the domain's use cases that follow it gives that setting a not-applicable reason. One following use case that gives the setting a value MUST be enough for the domain to owe the rule.

title: No obligation is silently left out of coverage
statement: Every obligation MUST count in at least one domain, or the workspace MUST say why not: a pattern that no use case follows, or an obligation that sits outside every domain, is reported as a warning.

title: A file that names the test's own ID accepts all the test's claims
statement: When an automated test's `file` names the test record's own ID, the engine MUST accept every record the test proves: the test record vouches for its own claims.

title: Otherwise the file names every ID the test proves
statement: When an automated test's file does not name the test's own ID and the test has no `key`, the file MUST name every ID the test proves (each target of a `proof`-role link). Naming one of them MUST NOT stand for the others, so that each claimed proof is checked.

title: A test's key replaces the ID rules
statement: When a test has a non-empty `key`, its file MUST contain that text exactly, and the ID rules of LA-TRC-DR11 and LA-TRC-DR12 MUST NOT apply. A key lets a test whose code names no ID, such as a dedicated pattern proof file, be checked by other text it must contain.

title: Only an automated test's file is checked for its claims
statement: The engine MUST check the claims of automated tests only. A manual or planned test's file, when it names one, is checked only for existing.

title: The unproved warnings and coverage count the same proof
statement: An obligation MUST be reported as `unproved` exactly when coverage does not count it as proved: an automated test's claim counts only when its file backs it, by naming the test's own ID, its `key`, or the obligation.

title: Proof owed by a planned test is never hidden by other proof
statement: An obligation that a planned test is meant to prove MUST count as proof still owed (`planned_any`) even when an automated or manual test already proves it. A planned test MUST NOT count as proof, so `planned_any` is never less than `planned` and never more than the total.

title: A test is counted once, in its own domain, by its state
statement: Each test record MUST be counted in exactly one domain's tests, the domain it sits in, under exactly one state: automated, manual or planned, which every test gives.

title: A domain owes proof of a pattern rule only through its own planned tests
statement: In each domain that owes a pattern rule, only a planned test in that domain makes the rule's proof owed there; a planned test in another domain that follows the same pattern MUST NOT.

title: A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every one of its rules
statement: When a domain `follows` a pattern itself, the domain MUST owe each of the pattern's rules, whatever its use cases give for the pattern's settings, since the domain's own follow cannot be marked not applicable. Only a rule with an applies-when setting that no follower there meets is waived; the domain counts as a follower, through the `setting_value` rows it gives.

title: A domain follows a pattern itself or through its use cases
statement: A domain MUST count as following a pattern when the domain itself or any of its use cases `follows` it. A rule owed both ways MUST be counted once in that domain.

title: A rule with no setting is owed wherever its pattern is followed
statement: A pattern rule that names no `setting` MUST be owed by every domain that follows its pattern, however it follows it.

title: A proof-only obligation is never asked for design
statement: An obligation of a proof-only kind MUST count as designed and built in every domain that owes it, MUST have no `satisfies` gap and MUST NOT be reported `unsatisfied`. Its proof MUST be counted, planned and reported as for any other obligation.

title: A use case that follows a pattern needs no requirements of its own
statement: A use case that `follows` an existing pattern MUST NOT be reported for having no requirements, since the pattern's rules state what it must do. A use case that follows no pattern and has no requirements MUST still be reported.

title: Every proof still owed is named, not only counted
statement: Every obligation that coverage counts in `planned_any` but not in `planned` MUST be named in a warning with the planned test that owes its proof, so the owed list and the count always agree.

title: Owed proof of a pattern rule is named in each domain that owes it
statement: A pattern rule MUST be named as still owed in a domain only when that domain owes the rule, a test in that domain proves it, and a planned test in that domain is also meant to prove it.

title: No test's proof silently counts nowhere
statement: A test whose every proof counts in no domain's coverage MUST be reported, with the reason for each target. A test's proof counts when its target is an obligation in a domain, or a pattern rule owed by the domain the test sits in. A test with at least one proof that counts MUST NOT be reported.

title: A manual test's file names the test
statement: A manual test's `file` MUST name the test's ID, an ID it proves, or its `key`, so that the steps a person follows say which test they carry out.

title: Support is never proof
statement: A `supports` link from a test MUST NOT count as proof or planned proof of its target in coverage, whatever the test's state, and its target need not appear in the test's file.

title: A test that only supports owes no ID in its file
statement: An automated test that proves no record but supports at least one MUST NOT be reported by `test-file-missing-id` for a file that names no ID. A `key` it has MUST still be found, and its `file` MUST still exist.

title: A key file is read in place of the test's file
statement: When a test names a `key_file`, its key, its own ID and the IDs it proves MUST be looked for in that file instead of its `file`, by every check and by coverage.

title: A key file is a file under the product root
statement: A test's `key_file` MUST name a file under the product root. One outside the root MUST be a `test-file-missing` error; a missing one MUST be a `test-file-missing` error, or a warning for a planned test, and no other check MAY report the test's key or IDs as missing from it.

title: Coverage shows every obligation kind the engine counts, and only what it counts
statement: A page that shows coverage MUST show every obligation kind the engine reports, in the engine's order (the schema's), and MUST NOT name obligation kinds of its own. A count the engine does not report MUST NOT be shown as zero.

title: A planned test never looks like proof
statement: Wherever a page shows a test, it MUST show the test's state. A planned test MUST look unfinished and MUST NOT be counted or drawn as proof.

title: A domain owes a pattern rule only through the use cases that follow it
statement: A pattern rule's status on a page MUST be worked out per domain: only a domain with a use case that follows the pattern owes the rule, and only components and tests in that domain count towards it, as the engine counts coverage. One domain's proof never counts for another.

title: Not applicable holds only when every following use case says so
statement: A pattern rule MUST be shown as not applicable in a domain only when it names a setting and every use case in that domain that follows the pattern gives that setting a not-applicable reason. If any one gives a value, the domain owes the rule.

title: Proof still owed is shown apart from proof
statement: Proof still owed by planned tests MUST be shown beside the planned count, never added to the proved count or drawn as part of the planned bar.

title: A gap callout repeats coverage's judgment
statement: A Traceability gap callout MUST come from coverage's own gaps for the domain that owes the obligation (and from the `component-file-missing` check for built), never from a count of links of its own, so it never disagrees with the coverage marks, the domain's Coverage line or the checks. A pattern rule is judged in each domain that owes it, from that domain's components and tests only.

title: Traceability groups follow the schema's roles
statement: Which links go in which Traceability group, and in what order, MUST follow only the schema: a relation's `design` or `proof` role, a test's `supports` links, and whether the record's kind is an obligation. A group is titled by its links' label, holds each record once, and is left out when empty.

title: A waived rule is neither owed nor proved
statement: A pattern rule waived in a domain, because no follower there gives a value that meets its applies-when setting, MUST NOT count in that domain at all: not as owed, designed, built or proved, and not as a gap. It stays owed in each other domain where a follower meets it.
